subject: Game Theory
title: The Medical Residency Match
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Medical Residency Match.

hook.text: Before 1952, hospitals poached med students earlier each year—some got offers as first-years. Chaos ensued.

buildup.text: The system collapsed: hospitals and students both gamed timing, breaking commitments and creating mismatches.

discovery.text: The National Resident Matching Program uses a centralized algorithm. Students rank hospitals, hospitals rank students.

twist.text: Roth redesigned it in the 1990s for couples wanting nearby placements. The updated algorithm finds stable matches.

climax.text: Over 40,000 doctors are matched yearly. It's considered the most successful application of mechanism design.

punchline.text: A centralized match beat decades of chaos.

quiz.question: What problem did the medical residency match solve?
options: Hospitals poaching students earlier each year
